assistant_text:
- General conservation formula (atom conservation form):
  For every element E, the total number of E atoms on the reactant side equals the total number on the product side:
  sum_over_reactants (a_{i,E} * n_i) = sum_over_products (a_{j,E} * n_j)

  Where:
  - n_i is the number of moles (or amount) of species i on the reactant side.
  - a_{i,E} is the number of atoms of element E in one molecule of species i.
  - The sums run over all reactant species i and all product species j in the balanced equation.

- What the inputs and outputs represent:
  - Inputs (reactants): the substances that enter the reaction. Their amounts (n_i) and their atomic composition (a_{i,E}) determine how many atoms of each element they contribute.
  - Outputs (products): the substances that are formed. Their amounts (n_j) and their atomic composition (a_{j,E}) determine how many atoms of each element they contain after the reaction.
  - The equation expresses that, for each element, the total number of that element on the left side (inputs) equals the total on the right side (outputs); this is the basis for balancing chemical equations and, more generally, for any conserved quantity such as mass.

- Quick example:
  2 H2 + O2 -> 2 H2O
  For element H: a(H2)=2 per molecule, n(H2)=2 => 2*2 = 4 H atoms on left; on right, H2O has 2 H per molecule, n(H2O)=2 => 2*2 = 4 H atoms.
  For element O: a(O2)=2 per molecule, n(O2)=1 => 2 O atoms on left; on right, H2O has 1 O per molecule, n(H2O)=2 => 2 O atoms.

- Note (alternative view): Mass conservation can be written similarly as ∑ m_i,in = ∑ m_j,out, where m_i = M_i * n_i (M_i is molar mass). The atom-conservation form is the more detailed version used for balancing reactions.
